chunks: And in the narration of al-Sakuni, he said:
Ali عليه السلام said: “The umm al-walad suffices in ẓihar.”

key_terms.أُمُّ الْوَلَدِ: a slave-woman who has borne her master's child
key_terms.السَّكُونِيِّ: al-Sakuni, the narrator through whom this report is transmitted
key_terms.الظِّهَارِ: ẓihar, the pre-Islamic form of declaring one's wife unlawful by likening her to one's mother
key_terms.تُجْزِي: is valid, sufficient, or fulfills the legal requirement
key_terms.عَلِيٌّ: Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام

ai.seo_question: Does an umm al-walad count in the rulings of ẓihar according to Imam Ali عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith conveys a legal ruling from Imam Ali عليه السلام concerning ẓihar. It states that an umm al-walad is valid or sufficient in the legal context of ẓihar, indicating her inclusion within its applicable rulings.
